title: Remuseum and the Doris Duke Foundation announce eight inaugural Vanguard Awardees
summary: Museum think tank Remuseum, in partnership with the Doris Duke Foundation, announces the inaugural class of awardees for The Vanguard: a first-of-its-kind incubator for innovative leaders in the visual and performing arts. Awardees’ organizations will each receive a $100,000 investment to carry out a new idea, and commit to a rigorous, year-long accelerator to build it into a practical model. Arts organizations celebrate artists who take risks but rarely give their leaders the capital or permission to do the same. Designed with faculty from MIT Sloan and the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, The Vanguard exists to correct that imbalance – to back leaders who are as creative as the artists whose work they present. The Vanguard begins with a week-long retreat at Shangri La — the Doris Duke Foundation’s global center for culture and ideas in Honolulu, HI — followed by a year of monthly coaching sessions, regional peer gatherings and collaborative wor

title: Pioneering 20th-century design dealer Anthony DeLorenzo's collection comes to Sotheby's
summary: Sotheby's will present DeLorenzo: The Legacy of a Design Champion, a landmark collection of more than 60 works from Anthony "Tony" DeLorenzo, the pioneering dealer who helped shape the American market for 20th-century design. Estimated at $4–6 million, the collection spans Tiffany Studios, French Art Deco, post-war and contemporary design, and American Studio Craft, reflecting a career defined by identifying extraordinary designers and movements long before they achieved widespread recognition. Over more than five decades, DeLorenzo introduced generations of collectors to artists and designers who would later become central to the international market. More than a survey of categories he helped champion, the collection offers a rare portrait of the curiosity, conviction and connoisseurship that defined his extraordinary career and that made him one of the most influential figures in the development of design collecting in the

title: Lévy Gorvy Dayan pairs Francis Bacon and Willem de Kooning in new New York exhibition
summary: Lévy Gorvy Dayan is presenting Bacon / de Kooning at 19 East 64th Street, New York. Taking place in the gallery's 1932 Beaux-Arts townhouse, the exhibition juxtaposes the works of Francis Bacon and Willem de Kooning, two indelible figures of postwar art. The presentation focuses on their smaller-scale paintings of the late 1960s and 1970s—de Kooning at primarily 60 by 55 inches, and Bacon at his preferred 14 by 12 inches—each chosen by the artists for their deliberately human proportions. Through these canvas dimensions, both painters could concentrate their emotive forces and demonstrate their respective technical and gestural virtuosities, reaching a shared essence of figuration and abstraction. Bacon and de Kooning famously encountered each other in 1975 in New York on the occasion of Bacon's retrospective at the Metropolitan Museum of Art—a face-to-face meeting commemorated by a now iconic photograph. title: Velázquez and court masterpieces anchor Prado exhibition on Queen Mariana of Austria
summary: The Museo Nacional del Prado and Fundación AXA are presenting Mariana of Austria, an exhibition that brings together more than one hundred works with the aim of analysing how art became an essential instrument for the representation and legitimisation of the authority of one of the most important political figures of the Hispanic Monarchy in the 17th century. Paintings, sculptures, prints and examples of the decorative arts reveal how Mariana of Austria asserted and projected her authority as queen consort, regent and queen mother in Early Modern Europe, with works by artists such as Velázquez, Martínez del Mazo, Carreño de Miranda and Claudio Coello. title: Damien Bachelot appointed president of Jeu de Paume
summary: Under the auspices of the French Ministry of Culture, the art centre's board of directors have elected Damien Bachelot as the new president of Jeu de Paume. Damien Bachelot is a specialist in corporate finance and investment banking. He has enjoyed a long career working in leading institutions within that sector and acted as chairman of the Aforge Finance Group, which he himself co-founded. Since the early 2000s, he and his wife Florence have amassed one of the largest private photography collections in France. Rooted in French humanist photography and American street photography, their collection has gradually expanded to incorporate more contemporary work. Today, it offers a special place to emerging French female photographers and champions the art of the photographic print by means of a dedicated prize. title: Hamburger Bahnhof launches a new online platform showcasing 30 recently acquired works in its collection
summary: With Dispatch, Hamburger Bahnhof is expanding its programme into the digital realm. Essays and videos exploring curatorial practice, theory, artistic practice, education and conservation introduce the themes and activities of the museum, offering insights into its research and work. From November 2026, Dispatch will bring the museum's practice into dialogue with current artistic positions and critical thinking on contemporary art. At its heart is the belief that sharing knowledge is a central responsibility of a public museum. To mark the 30th anniversary of Hamburger Bahnhof this year, the museum's innovative online platform presents 30 acquisitions and donations. It is freely accessible, with no registration required. A reading area and events at the museum will complement the digital offering. Dispatch is the digital extension of Hamburger Bahnhof's research and discourse

title: Whitney Museum presents a major survey of internet art exploring 25 years of artport
summary: The Whitney Museum of American Art presents artport: A History of Internet Art, a major exhibition marking the 25-year anniversary of artport, the Museum's online gallery space for net art commissions. artport: A History of Internet Art is the most comprehensive exhibition of web-based artworks to be presented in the United States in a museum setting. Since its launch in 2001, the platform has established the Whitney as a leader in the field of net art, supporting artists whose practices engage with an ever-evolving online environment. With more than 100 works commissioned specifically for the Whitney's online space, artport has played a key role in advancing the Museum's collection of digital and net art. For more than two decades, artport has provided a snapshot of the wide-ranging artistic practices on the internet, reflecting the ways artists have responded to changing technologies, evolving

title: Artipelag appoints Magnus af Petersens as new Chief Curator
summary: Artipelag has appointed one of Sweden's most internationally distinguished curators, Magnus af Petersens, as its new Chief Curator, effective December 1, 2026. With an extensive career at institutions including Moderna Museet, Bonniers Konsthall and Whitechapel Gallery in London, his appointment marks an important step in Artipelag's continued artistic development under its new Museum Director and CEO, Dragana K Maksimović. The appointment forms part of an ambitious strategy to further strengthen Artipelag's position as one of Europe's leading destinations for contemporary art and culture. Over several decades, Magnus af Petersens has played a prominent role in the Swedish and international art world. He has served as Senior Curator at Moderna Museet, Director of Bonniers Konsthall in Stockholm and Chief Curator at Whitechapel Gallery in London. title: Daniela Comani challenges the literary canon with "Orlando's Library" at Berlin's Kunstbibliothek
summary: The Kunstbibliothek of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin presents "Daniela Comani. Orlando's Library," a site-specific installation by the Italian artist that challenges established literary traditions and explores questions of gender, identity and cultural representation. On view in the foyer of the Kunstbibliothek at the Kulturforum, the special presentation runs from November 17, 2026, through March 8, 2027. Daniela Comani has created a site-specific work from her ongoing series "Orlando's Library" in the foyer of the Kunstbibliothek. The project stems from an invitation to the Italian artist to participate in BUCHSALON, a series of events organized by the Kunstbibliothek, in which Comani presents works from her extensive, internationally exhibited artistic practice, with a particular focus on the book as an artistic medium. title: Bode-Museum explores the dialogue between art, music and movement in "Sound Bodies"
summary: What does art sound like? How is music represented? And how do musical instruments combine sound and form? In the interactive exhibition "Sound Bodies", spread across all three levels of the Bode-Museum, historical and modern musical instruments enter into surprising dialogues with sculptures and other works of art related to music—from late-antique textiles from Egypt and medieval angel choirs to Antonio Canova's "Dancer." The exhibition runs from November 24, 2026, through March 7, 2027. Music connects people, times, and places. Drawing inspiration from the motto of the Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz, the Bode-Museum is exploring a theme that has permeated art and life since antiquity: music, the act of making music, and instruments—the sound bodies. title: Maja Bajević makes Zagreb solo debut with 'A Short Hystery of Our Time'
summary: The exhibition A short Hystery of Our Time presents the artistic oeuvre of Maja Bajević, one of the most internationally prominent artists from the former Yugoslavia since the 1990s. Her artistic practice is largely defined by the context of the wars in the territory of the former common state and by the experience of a gendered Bosnia and Herzegovina. At a time when radical right-wing political ideologies are gaining strength, opportunistically encouraging and mobilising the affects of division amid social and economic crises, Maja Bajević searches for ways to revive and re-articulate the revolutionary spirit that marked the progressive political upheavals of the 20th century. Rather than offering a black-and-white depiction of history, an attempt to reconstruct it, or a narrative of winners and losers, the artist emphasises the complexity of social reality, from which diverse, manifold interpretations of past

title: Exhibition at Maruani Mercier examines body and material as active partners in creation
summary: Bringing together works by Shawanda Corbett, Pam Glick, Naotaka Hiro, Emily Kraus and Brie Ruais, The Logic of Place considers the encounter between the artist’s body and material as a site of reciprocal exchange. Stepping away from the conventional view of the non-human world as passive and inert, the works in the exhibition variously position materials as vital players in the act of making. The surface and substance of canvas or clay envelop and touch the body, responding to and inflecting its movements, hesitations, and accelerations in space. Distinct modes of mark-making emerge throughout the exhibition, from the self-imposed logic of a gesture, to a set weight of material, to a mechanism that orients the body in close proximity to the canvas. Within these parameters, the process becomes dialogic – each action elicits a material response that, in turn, redirects the next movement. title: The year 2027 at the Ateneum is a celebration of Finnish art
summary: The Ateneum Art Museum will turn 140 in 2027, and the exhibitions that year will celebrate Finnish art. An extensive exhibition of works by Elin Danielson-Gambogi, to open in April, will be the first showcase of the artist’s entire career at the Ateneum, and it continues the museum’s efforts to highlight women artists. The exhibition Finlandia? – Finland constructed through art, to open in October, is a culmination of the Ateneum’s special year, and it is part of the programme celebrating the 110th anniversary of Finland’s independence. As part of the Modern Classics series, an exhibition of works by Alvar Cawén will open on 31 August. Elin Cleopatra Danielson-Gambogi (1861–1919) boldly followed her own path, living a bohemian life. title: Julien's Auctions and TCM Return with 'A Week of Hollywood Legends' This December
summary: This December, Julien’s Auctions and Turner Classic Movies (TCM) are lighting up the season with the return of “A Week of Hollywood Legends!” A spectacular array of over 1,000 screen objects from the most indelible films and television shows, blockbuster franchises, fan favorites and family classics, as well as exclusive collections from Classic to Contemporary Hollywood’s biggest stars will all come together at the ultimate destination for Hollywood memorabilia auctions’ year-end event taking place Monday, December 14th, Tuesday, December 15th, Wednesday, December 16th, Thursday, December 17th and Friday, December 18th (online only) at Julien’s Auctions in Los Angeles and online at Julien’s Auctions. title: Lofoten International Art Festival presents 2027 edition Children of the Sea-Wind
summary: A sanderling, a mackerel and an eel enter a Biennale. The sanderling takes a sculpture for a nest. The mackerel speaks in tongues nobody hears. The eel, refusing to represent anything, escapes down a drain. None of them has read Under the Sea-Wind, a book that marine biologist Rachel Carson wrote in 1941, ‘out of the deep conviction that the life of the sea is worth knowing.’ Moving across shores, waters and seasons, the book follows the lives of a sanderling, a mackerel and an eel, adopting their perspectives to narrate a world shaped by winds and currents. Coined by Carson, the term sea-wind acknowledges that the sea, the elements and the land are inseparable, that tides shape the edges of islands, waters carry memories and migratory animals connect places near and far. title: Palimpsest of African Cities explores the histories, memories and transformations of contemporary African urban life
summary: Presented as part of the OFF Programme of the 2026 Dakar Biennale and Partcours, "Palimpsest of African Cities" is a group exhibition bringing together artists, architects, photographers, filmmakers, and researchers to explore the forces, narratives, and everyday dynamics that shape contemporary African cities. The exhibition runs from November 20, 2026, through February 27, 2027. Conceived in partnership with KADIST, the African Artists' Foundation (AAF), and the Institut français du Sénégal, the exhibition approaches the city as a space in constant rewriting, where memories, everyday uses, architectures, mobilities, and imaginaries overlap and interact. title: Espoo Museum of Modern Art showcases 60 works by early studio ceramicist Gerda Thesleff
summary: A pioneering figure in modern Finnish ceramic art, Gerda Thesleff (1871–1939), takes centre stage in a new display, presented as part of the Collection Kakkonen exhibition at EMMA – Espoo Museum of Modern Art. Bringing together around 60 ceramic works, the small-scale exhibition introduces an artist whose distinctive visual language, experimental approach to ceramics and independent career shaped the development of ceramic art in Finland. Gerda Thesleff is on view from 25 November 2026 to 28 November 2027 within the Collection Kakkonen exhibition. Gerda Thesleff was among the earliest professional studio ceramicists in Finland and one of the first women to throw her own works. title: Museum Ludwig presents its 2027 program
summary: “In 2027, we are combining a close look at new images and media with an exploration of current social issues and historical works. Our collection of contemporary art on the basement level and in the main staircase forms the foundation of our institution. I look forward to a year of timely exhibitions that draw special attention to this foundation, while highlighting its historical context. The past shapes our understanding of the present, while the present opens up new perspectives on history. I warmly invite you to discover over the year new art and to see familiar works in a fresh light.“ —Director Yilmaz Dziewior AI tools now transform text and still images into videos that spread across social media within seconds. title: Mira M. Yang makes institutional solo debut in France with 'Ensemble' at Fondation Pernod Ricard
summary: The stage is a recurrent presence in Mira M. Yang’s work, appearing less as a space of illusion than a site where the unfinished and unresolved comes into light. It is a site of artifice, holding the potential for both liberation and estrangement, but also for exposing its own fictional nature. Mira M. Yang uses the stage as a means of inquiry into how cultural narratives are performed and constructed, and what lies beneath them, unresolved, hidden, and concealed. Theirs is a work about the unseen and unheard reappearing, but less as a conjuring of ghosts than a confrontation with what continues to haunt and affect our present and the ways in which cultural difference is staged. title: Carmézia Emiliano celebrates Macuxi culture and collective memory in new Sao Paulo exhibition
summary: Central presents "I Didn’t Come Alone," the first solo exhibition by Indigenous Brazilian artist Carmézia Emiliano at the gallery’s new space in Higienópolis, São Paulo. Opening on November 28, 2026, and continuing through February 13, 2027, the exhibition features three previously unseen monumental paintings accompanied by a critical essay by Lisette Lagnado. For four decades, Emiliano has devoted her artistic practice to painting and preserving the cultural memory of the Macuxi people. Through vibrant colors and richly populated compositions, the artist explores the traditions, mythology, ancestral knowledge and everyday experiences that define her community. Her paintings depict activities such as hunting, fishing, preparing cassava, weaving nets and firing clay pots, alongside social gatherings, festivities and collective practices. An

title: Heritage's wine auction offers historic 1973 Chateau Montelena Chardonnay
summary: A bottle of the California Chardonnay that helped change the course of wine history will take the spotlight alongside major estate-direct consignments in Heritage’s Dec. 11 Fine & Rare Wine Signature® Auction. The 1973 Chateau Montelena Chardonnay, which famously placed first among the white wines at the 1976 Judgment of Paris, was consigned by the winery’s estate director, George Blanckensee, and bears the signatures of five figures connected to the legendary blind tasting: Jim Barrett, Bo Barrett, Mike Grgich, George Taber, and Steven Spurrier. The offering arrives in the 50th-anniversary year of the competition that challenged French wine’s supremacy and brought international recognition to California producers. title: RM Sotheby's establishes motorsport records during €12.1 million Munich sale
summary: RM Sotheby’s Munich Auction achieved total sales of €12,101,700, with a sell-through rate of 92 per cent, as two Mercedes-Benz DTM competition cars established new auction records. Returning to Motorworld for its fifth year, RM Sotheby’s Munich auction once again took its place at the heart of Germany’s collector car market, attracting strong interest across a diverse selection of significant automobiles. Two Mercedes-Benz DTM cars proved among the highlights of the evening, each achieving a new auction record. A 2014 Mercedes-AMG C-Coupé sparked one of the night's most spirited bidding battles, with two telephone bidders competing for the HWA-built racer. Driven by former Formula 1 driver Paul di Resta, the car recorded a best finish of third at Hockenheim before achieving €938,750, comfortably exceeding its low estimate

title: Rare lichen found in New York's Adirondack forests for the first time
summary: A previously undetected lichen has been documented for the first time in New York State and the contiguous United States, broadening our understanding of the biodiversity of the state’s forests. The tiny lichen, Sclerophora coniophaea, was found by a graduate student working with scientists from the New York State Museum and SUNY College of Environmental Science and Forestry (ESF), as part of an Environmental Protection Fund (EPF) funded research project initiated by the New York State Department of Conservation (NYSDEC). Jeremy Howland, a graduate student at the City University of New York (CUNY) and a research associate at the New York State Museum in Albany, made the observation as part of a larger effort to study mature and old-growth forests across New York’s Forest Preserve.
